title: Hardik-Arshdeep Swap Nears Completion as Mumbai, Punjab Exchange Formal Interest
excerpt: Cricbuzz reports both franchises have exchanged Expressions of Interest and both players have consented, leaving only contract exchange and BCCI confirmation — with no third player involved.
body:
• The proposed Hardik Pandya–Arshdeep Singh trade between Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings is nearing completion: the franchises have exchanged Expressions of Interest under the BCCI process, Cricbuzz reports.
  • Both players are understood to have consented, leaving only the exchange of contracts and formal BCCI confirmation.
  • As things stand, no third player is involved — narrowing earlier reports that had wicketkeeper-batter Vishnu Vinod moving to Mumbai as part of the deal.
  • If confirmed, Hardik would play under Shreyas Iyer at Punjab, ending three seasons as Mumbai captain, while Arshdeep would pair with Jasprit Bumrah in Mumbai's attack.

The blockbuster IPL trade sending Hardik Pandya to Punjab Kings and Arshdeep Singh to Mumbai Indians has moved into its final stage. Cricbuzz reports that the two franchises have exchanged Expressions of Interest (EoIs) under the process prescribed by the Board of Control for Cricket in India, that both players have consented to the trade, and that the exchange of contracts is all that remains before formal BCCI confirmation.

What is new

Two things have changed since the talks were first reported on November 3. First, the pause is over: the deal had briefly stalled, with Pandya understood to have sought some time before deciding, but that is now resolved and the all-rounder is believed to have agreed to the move. Second, the shape of the deal has narrowed. Cricbuzz says there is no indication of a third player being involved — which supersedes the earlier version of the story, reported by Sportstar and others, in which Punjab wicketkeeper-batter Vishnu Vinod would also have moved to Mumbai. On the latest reporting, this is a straight one-for-one swap of two India internationals.

How the trade process works

Under the BCCI framework, once EoIs are exchanged the board formally allows the franchises to engage with each other's players; once the players consent and the financial terms are agreed, the contracts are exchanged and the trade can be confirmed. The IPL's trade rules are explicit about the gate:

"Only players whose names are included on an EOI Confirmation and for whom a signed Consent Form has been received by the BCCI may be traded."

— IPL trade rules, quoted by Cricbuzz

Cricbuzz adds that any delay in the official announcement could be on account of the ongoing festivities and official holidays in India, and that confirmation is expected shortly. Neither franchise has yet announced the trade itself, so until the BCCI confirms it, this remains a reported deal in its final formalities — not an official one.

Why Mumbai want Arshdeep, and what Punjab get

The cricket logic is clearest on Mumbai's side. Cricbuzz reports that Mumbai have been looking for a quality bowler to complement Jasprit Bumrah, a need sharpened after new-ball options Trent Boult and Deepak Chahar had relatively underwhelming campaigns in the last IPL. Arshdeep is regarded as India's leading new-ball and death-overs bowler after Bumrah. He is also Punjab's all-time highest wicket-taker in the IPL, and Punjab had retained him at the 2025 auction for Rs 18 crore by exercising their Right to Match card — which underlines how much they are giving up. Punjab's return is Hardik himself: an all-rounder of proven title-winning pedigree whose experience, Cricbuzz notes, could add considerable value to a side still chasing its first IPL triumph, having reached only two finals in 19 years, in 2014 and 2025.

The captaincy question

For Hardik, the move ends a five-year run as a franchise captain — two seasons leading Gujarat Titans, then the last three in charge of Mumbai Indians. At Punjab, that role is not waiting for him: Shreyas Iyer has been firmly established as the side's leader over the last two seasons. Hardik is, however, regarded as a team player with a reputation for bringing the best out of younger players, and he would arrive as the senior all-rounder in Iyer's team rather than as its captain. Mumbai, meanwhile, have separately made clear that Suryakumar Yadav is not part of any trade discussion.

What happens next

The remaining steps are administrative: contracts exchanged, then BCCI confirmation and the franchises' announcements. Until those land, IPL 2027 planning for both squads sits in limbo — Mumbai cannot build their pace attack around Arshdeep, and Punjab cannot plan their middle order around Hardik. On Cricbuzz's reporting, that wait should be short.
